images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A graphite filing cabinet, about the height of a shoebox on end, stands at the right of a pale neutral tabletop, its top drawer pulled open to show a row of ivory folders with unmarked tabs. On the desk in front of it lies a single thick employee file, an ivory folder with crisp creases, holding a blank photo card and ruled sheets. Beside it rests a graphite ID badge on a coiled frosted acrylic lanyard, its acid-lime access strip glowing softly. To the left, a small graphite doorframe stands closed with a frosted-glass badge reader beside it. A mug with a faint coffee ring sits by the file. Fine dust rests in the drawer rails, and fibres show at the folder's edges. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

A flat graphite sweeper arm slides across the desk from the left, having wiped that half bare, and is pushing the mug off the edge, the lanyard sliding after it. Paper dust hangs in a column above the empty folder. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. In the midground, a slim graphite archive rig runs along overhead rails, its lime folder clamp holding one rebuilt ivory file with its sheets restacked, lowering it into the reopened slot of a single cleaned drawer. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents.
